answer: Linear stake-weighted rewards make splitting accounts unprofitable. For grove surveys, nectar sampling and voyage reports, distribute a fixed reward pool in proportion to capital locked for the full epoch, with no per-account bonus. A verifier uses the epoch's locked-balance snapshot; the same funds cannot back two claims. An attacker sacrifices liquidity, and dividing one stake among N accounts leaves its total reward share unchanged. This assumes strictly linear weights and no minimum payout per identity.
